stories.title: New Deputy Election Commissioner appointed in ECI amid concerns over work hierarchy
stories.summary: Prakash Rajpurohit fills the vacancy left by Sanjay Kumar’s premature repatriation, amid concerns raised by Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over IT department files not being routed through him
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Prakash Rajpurohit, an IAS officer of the 2010 batch, has been appointed as a Deputy Election Commissioner in the Election Commission of India (ECI), filling the vacancy caused by the premature repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, who was incharge of the Electoral Rolls and IT division.

What will be the work allocation in the ECI after this new appointment is crucial, as Sanjay Kumar, who had been DEC from August 2024 till August this year, had been responsible for the electoral roll and IT divisions of the ECI, and had signed the ECI’s June 24, 2025, order initiating the SIR in the country.
It is also important because the two Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had written to the Cabinet Secretary on how files of the ECI.
IT department head Dr. Seema Khanna not being routed through Mr. Kumar, who was a seasoned officer, was a violation.
Dr. Khanna joined the ECI in 2025 on deputation from the National Informatics Centre.
She heads the commission’s.
IT department, and oversees its digital infrastructure, including systems for electoral-roll management.

According to Election Commission sources, before the repatriation of Sanjay Kumar to his parent cadre, Dr. Khanna’s files had been routed through him till she was given a promotion to Level 15, which is equivalent to the rank of an Additional Secretary.

Since Mr. Kumar was of the rank of a Joint Secretary (which is Level 14), Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg issued an internal order that Dr. Khanna’s files should go straight to the Election Commissioners from then.
This order was, however, never implemented.

Dr. Khanna’s files started being routed through to Maneesh Garg himself following the repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, as he was his link officer, which made him responsible for his departments in his absence.
Mr. Rajpurohit’s appointment was cleared by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet late on Saturday as per the order by the Department of Personnel and Training.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court-appointed High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) has launched a portal to enquire into all aspects of the incidents relating to violence at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, and at places outside Delhi, during the month of July 2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said on Saturday (October 17, 2026).

The MHA said that priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence, harassment of female protestors, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side.
“The portal, http://hpec.nic.in, has been launched for the convenience of the affected people, including police personnel,” it said.
The Committee will examine issues outlined in the Supreme Court’s order.
“The portal has been designed to protect vulnerable witnesses and allow affected people to keep their identities confidential, if they wish to do so,” it said.
“Affected people and other stakeholders have been encouraged to submit complaints and representations through the portal using the applicable formats,” the MHA said.
Anyone wishing to provide information or suggestions on issues referred to the Committee under the two court orders can also use the portal.

“Complaints, representations and other relevant material can also be submitted in person at the Committee’s office at Shiksha Sadan, 17 Rouse Avenue Institutional Area, New Delhi, between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. on working days,” it said.
“Submissions can also be sent by post to the same address or by email to hpec2026.enquiry@nic.in,” it said.

Supreme Court had constituted a five-member HPEC to enquire into all aspects of the incidents of violence at Jantar Mantar in Delhi and at places outside the national capital during July 2026, including the broader issues surrounding the incidents.

Besides Justice Reddy, the Committee comprises former Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi High Court judge Justice Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya DGP L.R. Bishnoi.

The Supreme Court ordered the constitution of the Committee while hearing a batch of pleas alleging police excesses against student protesters during the agitation spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), alongside allegations of violence against police personnel.

Addressing the 34th annual convocation of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) here, he said legal education must go beyond academic learning and prepare students to engage with diverse perspectives and serve society.
"I greet you not only with congratulations but also with immense expectations," the CJI said.

Emphasising the responsibilities of the legal profession, Surya Kant said it required not only knowledge of statutes and precedents but also the courage to stand up for justice.

stories.headline: Supreme Court declares internet access a fundamental right for children
stories.title: Supreme Court declares internet access a fundamental right for children
stories.summary: Supreme Court declares internet access a fundamental right for children
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court affirmed children's internet rights and ordered a national CSEAM database.
The ruling favours proportionate online safeguards over blanket age-based restrictions.

The Supreme Court has declared access to and use of the internet a fundamental right of children and directed the Centre to create a national database to detect and remove sexually explicit visual content depicting minors from digital platforms, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
The court issued the order while hearing a petition highlighting an alarming increase in child sexual exploitation and abuse material, or CSEAM, circulating on social media platforms.
It also issued several directions aimed at curbing the rise of such content on social media and other online platforms.
A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the internet was the marketplace of ideas, creative expression and information.
Its value lay not only in the information it contained but also in the access it provided to adults and children, the bench said.

“In view of the foregoing, we have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.

Our children, irrespective of their age, enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing,” the court said in its 137-page order passed on October 15.
According to PTI, the order came on a petition filed by the NGO Just Rights for Children Alliance, which works in the areas of child sexual exploitation, child trafficking and child marriage.
Senior advocate HS Phoolka represented the organisation.
The court said its observations did not mean that age-based restrictions should be ruled out.

article_sentences: Kolkata: The father of the junior doctor who was raped and murdered at Kolkata’s state-run RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in August 2024 on Saturday threatened to launch a fresh movement in West Bengal following the Supreme Court’s decision to grant bail to former hospital principal Sandip Ghosh in a financial irregularities case.
A Supreme Court division bench comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B Varale on Friday granted bail to Ghosh, citing his prolonged incarceration and the slow pace of the trial.
“I will see it through to the end.
Even if necessary, I will call for a fresh movement in the state on this issue and hit the streets,” Sekhar Debnath, father of the junior doctor, told mediapersons.

Asked whether a fresh agitation would amount to a protest against the current BJP-led state government, particularly when his wife, Ratna Debnath, the victim’s mother, is a legislator of the ruling party, he said the political circumstances would not deter him from seeking justice for his daughter.
“It really does not matter that she is a part of the ruling dispensation.
I will do whatever is necessary for justice,” the victim’s father said.

Information about alleged large-scale financial irregularities at RG Kar, where Ghosh was the principal during the previous Trinamool Congress government led by Mamata Banerjee, surfaced after the junior doctor’s rape and murder in August 2024.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Ghosh in connection with alleged corruption at the state-run medical institution.
The victim’s parents had subsequently alleged that influential people were involved in their daughter’s death.
Debnath has now warned that he could return to the streets to protest against the latest development, renewing his demand for justice.
Ghosh had approached the Supreme Court after the Calcutta High Court rejected his bail plea.

stories.headline: India gets tariff reprieve as Trump waives Russian oil penalties, but the threat lingers
stories.title: India gets tariff reprieve as Trump waives Russian oil penalties, but the threat lingers
stories.summary: Delhi’s energy sourcing stays guided by national interest; experts warn threat of revived tariffs could be used as leverage in trade talks
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive punitive tariffs on countries buying Russian oil and gas gives India relief from the threat of additional duties of up to 100 per cent on its exports to the US.
But it leaves Washington with the option of reviving the penalties, potentially using them as leverage in ongoing bilateral trade agreement (BTA) negotiations, experts noted.

New Delhi’s position on sourcing crude oil from Moscow and other countries will continue to be guided by its national interest and energy security, even as the order provides for continued US monitoring of Russian oil purchases and allows US President Donald Trump to withdraw the waiver and reimpose punitive tariffs, sources tracking the matter told businessline.

“Indian officials had been in discussions with their US counterparts over the implications of the legislation and the possibility of a waiver and there was optimism that it would happen after Trump struck a diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to supply the American and global markets with Russian refined fuel.
New Delhi’s stance on sourcing energy based on its national interest remains unchanged and interactions with Washington would continue,” the source said.
For India, the waiver buys time to negotiate a trade deal but offers no lasting certainty, pointed out Ajay Srivastava from trade research body GTRI.

Despite Russia’s share of Indian oil imports declining from 51 per cent in July to 44 per cent in August, as India bought more from the US and from the UAE, Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (SRIA) remains law leaving Washington free to revive the tariff threat to extract concessions in bilateral trade talks.
“India should protect its energy security, buy oil on commercial terms and prepare for renewed US pressure.
Temporary tariff relief is no basis for permanent trade concessions,” Srivastava said.
In an executive order dated October 16, Trump waived the duties and several sanctions provisions under the Lindsey O. Graham SRIA, which he signed into law on September 18.

The order provides for a 100 per cent increase in the rate of duty on goods from the five largest importers of Russian-origin crude oil and natural gas if they knowingly make new purchases from October 18.

It also provides for a 500 per cent increase in duties on Russian goods and 100 per cent increases for the five largest facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion, subject to the specified exceptions and waivers.

article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday issued notice to the Centre on a plea seeking a comprehensive and enforceable regulatory framework to protect children from the risks associated with social media platforms, including age-based restrictions on access and safeguards against online exploitation.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on the petition filed by The Emerald Heights International School and its Director (Academics), Siddharth Singh Girnar, and tagged it with a pending petition raising a similar issue.
The apex court has listed the matter for further hearing on December 3.

The petition, filed against the Union of India, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Ministry of Law and Justice, and the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, raises concerns over unrestricted access to commercial social media platforms by children and the alleged inadequacy of the existing legal and regulatory framework to address the risks posed by their use.

stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea Challenging Allahabad HC Order Banning Hookah Bars In Restaurants
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently issued notice to the State of Uttar Pradesh in a plea challenging the Allahabad High Court's order, which held that hookah bars and hookah services can not be provided even in "Designated Smoking Areas".

Vide order dated September 29, a bench of Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary dismissed a batch of connected petitions concerning the operation of hookah bars and the provision of hookah services in restaurants.

It held that hookah service in a Designated Smoking Area is also prohibited under Rule 4(3) of the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008, as amended in 2017, read with the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, 2003 (COTPA).
A bench comprising Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe issued notice on a special leave petition filed by M/S. Good Luck Food And Beverages challenging the High Court's judgment.
It has also issued notice on a prayer for interim relief.
The High Court stressed that the right of non-smokers to breathe clean air in a public place cannot be abridged by the commercial interests of an establishment claiming a right to trade.
The issue before the High Court was not whether smoking tobacco through a hookah, in isolation, was prohibited.
The question was whether restaurants and similar establishments could provide hookah as a service in a Designated Smoking Area.
The High Court observed that the general rule under COTPA is prohibition of smoking in public places, while the Designated Smoking Area is an exception to that general prohibition.

It further noted that while a Designated Smoking Area permits smoking, it does not permit a restaurant to provide hookah service, because the amended Rule 4(3) prohibits "any service" in a smoking area.

Ultimately, the bench held that "operation of hookah bars and rendering of hookah services by restaurants in the State of Uttar Pradesh" is a flagrant violation of Rule 4(3) and contrary to the scheme and object of COTPA.
The High Court heavily relied on the 2017 amendment to Rule 4(3).

stories.headline: HDFC deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha announces exit ahead of Anup Bagchi's takeover as CEO
stories.title: HDFC deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha announces exit ahead of Anup Bagchi's takeover as CEO
stories.summary: HDFC Bank's Deputy Managing Director, Kaizad Bharucha, has announced his resignation, effective December 31. This move precedes Anup Bagchi's appointment as the new Managing Director and CEO. In the latest reports, HDFC Bank has demonstrated remarkable profitability shifts this July to September, reflecting improved asset quality and a surge in net profit. Bharucha's resignation awaits approval from the Reserve Bank of India, as it has been accepted by the board.

stories.headline: Delhi court issues bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee
stories.title: Delhi court issues bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 17 : A Delhi court has issued a bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in an eight-year-old criminal defamation case filed by Vikas Pandey, after being informed that a fresh summons issued could not be served as the premises of his residence was found locked. The Saket Courts passed the order on Saturday after being apprised that the service of summons on Rathee remained incomplete. The court has now listed the matter for further hearing on October 31. In an order passed earlier this month, the court had permitted fresh summons to be served on Rathee through dasti service, allowing the complainant to accompany the process server to facilitate service. Despite the steps taken, the court was informed that the notice could not be served as the premises of Rathee's house was locked, leading to the issuance of the bailable warrant. The case pertains to a video titled 'BJP IT Cell Part 2', which allegedly defamed Pandey. The video was also retweeted by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal in 2018, who later acknowledged before the Supreme Court that he had made a mistake by retweeting it. Pandey, the founder of the social media page 'I Support Narendra Modi', had claimed that the retweet had tarnished his reputation. The proceedings against Rathee had remained pending amid repeated difficulties in serving summons on him since 2019, with the complainant claiming that his continued absence from India had delayed the case. Rathee ordinarily resides in Austria. The matter had also reached the Supreme Court in connection with Kejriwal's challenge to the criminal defamation proceedings arising from the retweet. In February 2024, Kejriwal told the apex court that he had made a mistake by sharing the video. A Bench of Justices Sanjiv Khanna, who later became Chief Justice of India (CJI) and has since retired, and Dipankar Datta had stayed the trial court proceedings against Kejriwal while hearing his plea challenging the Delhi High Court's refusal to quash the summons issued against him. The Delhi High Court had earlier upheld the summoning order, observing that retweeting allegedly defamatory content could attract prosecution under Section 499 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). --IANS

stories.headline: Non-Tariff Barriers Biggest Hurdle in India-China Trade: Nirmala Sitharaman
stories.title: Non-Tariff Barriers Biggest Hurdle in India-China Trade: Nirmala Sitharaman
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Bangkok: Non-tariff barriers remain the single biggest obstacle in trade ties between India and China, Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman said on Friday, pointing out that an expanding trade imbalance continues to weigh heavily against the country despite years of bilateral engagement.

The Minister made these observations during an interactive session with Michael Kugelman of the Atlantic Council on 'India's economic edge', held on the sidelines of the World Bank-IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.
Addressing the trade friction with Beijing, Sitharaman said that, "So non-tariff barriers are the biggest hurdle in the trade between India and China.

That is one, and second, if the approach globally that you see today, where imbalance is huge, countries impose tariffs and say, 'no, we cannot sustain this imbalance, either you correct it or else we are going to be very punitive on you', that approach we have never taken." Sitharaman mentioned that with China, the trade balance is against India' and it is growing exponentially.
She noted that Indian products face persistent roadblocks across key sectors despite proven global competitiveness.
"We are global leaders in generic drugs, bovine meat, vegetables and perishables and very many such goods which have huge potential in China.
I would think a decade has gone by, consistently putting up a case for market access for Indian products.

But non-tariff barriers have been very strong and China uses non-tariff barriers unhesitatingly, whether it is in the name of phytosanitary measures or any other, for which due investigations can happen, for which due both sides sitting and talking can happen, but no progress is made," the Minister said.
